name: Complement Component 4 Deficiency

criteria.description: Persistently low or undetectable serum complement C4 levels
History of recurrent bacterial infections, especially with encapsulated organisms
Presence of autoimmune disease manifestations such as systemic lupus erythematosus
Identification of mutations or deletions in the C4A or C4B genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistently low C4 levels plus either recurrent infections or autoimmune manifestations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by genetic testing and exclusion of other complement deficiencies.

common.symptomName: Autoimmune manifestations (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus-like symptoms)

laboratory: Low or absent serum C4 complement levels
Normal or low C3 complement levels
Positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) in autoimmune cases
Elevated inflammatory markers during infections or autoimmune flares
imaging: Renal ultrasound or biopsy findings consistent with glomerulonephritis
MRI brain in cases with CNS vasculitis
genetic: Mutations or deletions in C4A or C4B genes detected by molecular genetic testing
other: Family history of complement deficiencies or autoimmune diseases

distinguishingFeatures: Low C2 levels with normal or mildly decreased C4

redFlags: Severe recurrent infections with encapsulated bacteria
Early onset systemic lupus erythematosus-like autoimmune disease
references: Walport MJ. Complement. First of two parts. N Engl J Med. 2001 Apr 5;344(14):1058-66.
Pickering MC, Botto M. Complement and disease: lessons from complement deficiencies. Mol Immunol. 2001 Nov;38(2-3):161-74.
Miyagawa S, et al. Complement C4 deficiency and autoimmune diseases. Clin Exp Immunol. 2019;198(3):345-355.
